chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Hamran, from al-Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, when Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, intends good for a servant, He marks a spot of light in his heart, opens the pores of his heart, and assigns an angel to guide him. And when He intends evil for a servant, He marks a black spot in his heart, closes the pores of his heart, and assigns a demon to mislead him,
So whoever Allah intends to guide, He expands his breast for Islam; and whoever He intends to cause to err, He makes his breast strait and narrow, as though he were ascending upwards.

He said: Then he recited this verse. The Compiler of this book said: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, intends evil for a servant as a result of a sin he commits, thereby deserving that a seal be placed on his heart and a demon be assigned to mislead him. And He does not do this to him except by deserving it. And sometimes Allah, the Mighty and High, assigns an angel to guide His servant by deserving it or by favor, and He singles out for His mercy whom He wills,
And Allah, the Mighty and High, says: 'And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Compassionate, We appoint for him a demon, so he becomes his associate.'
ai.seo_question: How does God guide or mislead individuals according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid elucidates the metaphysical mechanism of divine guidance (hidayah) and misguidance (dalal), attributing the 'marking' of the heart to God's will while the compiler, al-Saduq, contextualizes misguidance as a just consequence of sin (istihqaq) rather than arbitrary decree. It highlights the role of angelic support for the guided and demonic companionship for the misguided, reinforcing the Shia understanding of divine justice and the interplay between human agency and divine grace.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 14. My father (RA) said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abu `UImayr, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Humran, on the Sulayman ibn Khalid that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Verily, if Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, intends good for a servant, then He places a spot of light in his heart, expands the hearing of his heart, and assigns an angel over him to direct him. If He intends evil for a servant, He places a black sport in his heart, blocks the hearing of his heart, and assigns a demon over him to misled him.”

The he (AS) recited this verse: Therefore, (for) whomsoever Allah intends that He would guide him aright, He expands his breast for Islam, and (for) whomsoever He intends that He should cause him to err, He makes his breast strait and narrow as though he were ascending upwards.

The Compiler of this book says: Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, intends evil for a servant as a result of a sin that he has committed. As a result, his heart receives the stamp, and a demon is assigned to mislead him. Allah only does this to those who deserve it. And sometimes Allah assigns an angel over His Servant to dir4ect him according to what he has earned, and as part of Allah`s favor. Allah is Merciful towards whomsoever He pleases.
Allah, the Mighty and High, says: And whoever turns himself away from the remembrance of the Most Compassionate, We appoint fro him a Shaytan, so he becomes his associate.
